chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: May a man perform the prayers of the night and the day all of them with one tayammum? He said: Yes, so long as he does not enter a state of ritual invalidation or find water. I said: If he finds water and hopes that he will be able to obtain other water, and he thinks that he will be able to get it, but when he wants it that becomes difficult for him? He said: That nullifies his tayammum, and he must repeat the tayammum.
On the basis that it is possible to interpret it as a type of recommendation, like renewing wudu (ablution) for every salat (prayer), and that it is a completion.

key_terms.النَّهَارِ: the daytime period, here referring to the day prayers
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, whose availability affects the validity of tayammum
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the standard ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَيَمُّمٍ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl when water is unavailable
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: nullifies or breaks the prior state of ritual substitute purification
key_terms.يُحْدِثْ: to enter a state that invalidates ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Can one tayammum be used for multiple daily prayers in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of tayammum and whether one tayammum suffices for multiple prayers. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that one tayammum remains valid for the prayers of night and day unless it is invalidated by ritual occurrence or by finding water. The closing note indicates that redoing tayammum in the later case may be understood as recommended rather than strictly obligatory.
